data.title: Smaller motors, cheaper EVs? ZF’s 30,000rpm electric drive targets mainstream cars
data.description:
A new electric drive from German automotive supplier ZF is claimed to make EV motors smaller, lighter and cheaper without sacrificing power, potentially giving car-makers more room to work with and less expensive hardware to install.

Called the High Revolution Drive, the system spins its motor at up to 30,000rpm and is aimed at high-volume passenger cars with outputs of around 150-200kW, rather than being reserved for exotic performance models.

ZF claims the complete drive is almost 25 per cent smaller and lighter than a comparable unit from its existing SELECT family, while requiring half the magnet mass. Its product page also claims approximately 13 per cent lower system costs.

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

Those are potentially meaningful savings for manufacturers trying to make electric cars more affordable, although a cheaper drive unit does not translate into an equivalent percentage reduction in the showroom price.

ZF is talking to several car-makers and targeting production by 2030.

The significance lies less in chasing a headline motor speed than in combining that speed with lower material use, compact packaging and efficiency comparable to the larger drive it could replace.

High-revving electric motors are already part of the industry’s development push. Xiaomi, for example, quotes speeds of up to 27,200rpm for its HyperEngine technology, showing ZF is advancing an established engineering approach rather than inventing a new way to propel an EV.

What makes ZF’s proposal noteworthy is its focus on the mainstream market and the claimed savings across the integrated drive system, which combines the motor, inverter and transmission.

The principle behind the smaller motor is straightforward. Power depends on both torque and rotational speed, so spinning faster allows a motor to produce the same power with less torque.

That enables a smaller motor, while reduction gearing converts its high-speed rotation into the torque needed to turn the wheels.

ZF uses two stages of reduction gearing with an overall ratio of about 18:1. The version it has shown produces a peak 200kW and 3500Nm at the wheels.

That wheel-torque figure is measured after the gearing multiplies the motor’s torque, so it should not be compared directly with the motor-torque figures normally quoted in EV specifications.

Similarly, the two-stage transmission refers to successive stages of reduction gearing; it does not establish that the vehicle has a two-speed gearbox that changes gear while driving.

ZF’s comparison is with a SELECT drive whose motor reaches 18,000rpm. The new unit’s 30,000rpm ceiling represents an increase of about 67 per cent.

Making that work presents challenges in controlling noise and vibration, which ZF says it has addressed by developing the motor, gearing, bearings and gear-tooth geometry together.

The company’s transmission experience is relevant here: making a motor spin faster is only useful if the complete drive remains quiet, durable and efficient enough for everyday cars.

ZF says the system achieves nearly 93 per cent efficiency, comparable with the existing SELECT drive.

That qualification matters when assessing the range potential. ZF is claiming a smaller and lighter drive with similar efficiency, rather than a large reduction in the electricity needed to deliver the same mechanical output.

Reducing weight could help driving range, and the smaller package could give vehicle designers more flexibility. However, ZF has not quantified an extra distance per charge or specified the weight saving in kilograms.

Nor does a drive unit that is 25 per cent lighter make the entire car 25 per cent lighter: the battery, body and other components still account for much of an EV’s mass.

The reduction in magnet requirements could be particularly useful commercially, cutting material costs and exposure to critical supply chains. ZF also identifies lower copper and iron consumption on its product page.

The High Revolution Drive is being developed as a variant of the modular SELECT platform, using existing technologies to limit development work and allow manufacturers to tailor it to different vehicles.

Its architecture can accommodate both 400-volt and 800-volt electrical systems, broadening the range of potential applications beyond cars using the latest high-voltage platforms.

data.title: Mercedes-AMG GT SUV Deep Dive: Why heat matters more than horsepower in this electric monster
data.description:
The Mercedes-AMG GT SUV can produce a staggering 860kW. But the more interesting question is what happens after the first few seconds of full-throttle acceleration.

Delivering enormous power in an electric vehicle is one challenge. Delivering it repeatedly, without the motors, battery and electronics overheating and forcing a reduction in output, is quite another.

That’s the engineering problem AMG is tackling with its new electric performance flagship. Alongside its 860kW peak output, the GT 63 SUV is rated at 530kW continuously, with an arsenal of compact axial-flux motors, individually cooled battery cells and sophisticated thermal management designed to keep the performance coming.

READ MORE: Best luxury EVs in Australia 2026: Premium electric cars under $100k, $150k, $250k and beyond, priced and compared

READ MORE: Unveiled: The new Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door EV has so much tech it makes the Porsche Taycan look very yesterday
READ MORE: Is this the sensible supercar? Mercedes-AMG GT 53 EV revealed with less power but 112km more range than crazy axial-flux 860kW flagship
READ MORE: 2026 Porsche Cayenne Turbo EV Brief Drive: This vehicle is brilliant, but all sorts of wrong

The technology is significant beyond the headline numbers, although how effectively it works remains to be established in independent testing.

Mercedes-Benz Australia lists the GT SUV as coming soon, with local pricing and specifications still to be confirmed.

The GT SUV range comprises three all-wheel drive models. The entry-level GT 53 produces 400kW and 800Nm from two conventional electric motors, while the GT 55 steps up to three axial-flux motors producing 600kW and 1860Nm.

The flagship GT 63 uses the same three-motor configuration but increases peak output to 860kW and 2000Nm.

The GT 55 and GT 63 share a claimed continuous output of 530kW, despite their substantially different peak ratings.

All three models use 800-volt electrical architecture, with battery capacities of 106kWh or 128kWh depending on the variant.

Where the heat comes from

An EV converts stored electrical energy into motion through its battery, inverters and motors. Each stage incurs losses, some of which become heat that must be removed.

A short acceleration run can use some of the system’s capacity to absorb heat. Repeated acceleration or sustained high speed requires heat to be carried away quickly enough to prevent temperatures continually rising.

Cooling from inside the battery outwards

The battery’s ability to deliver power depends partly on the temperature of individual cells. An acceptable average pack temperature can conceal a local hot spot that forces the control system to reduce output.

Many liquid-cooled EV batteries transfer heat through a plate or other cooling structure adjoining the cells. AMG instead circulates electrically non-conductive oil directly around each cylindrical cell.

Both approaches must conduct heat out of the cell’s interior. Direct cooling brings the fluid to the cell casing, reducing the intervening structures through which that heat must pass.

AMG also uses narrow cells, measuring 26mm across and 105mm tall. Their diameter limits the distance between the core and the cooled outer surface. An aluminium casing helps conduct heat, while a full-tab design reduces internal electrical resistance, according to the company.

Moving heat is only the first step

Oil passing around the cells carries heat away from them, but the vehicle still has to dispose of that heat. Cooling capacity is also needed by the motors and their power electronics.

AMG’s Central Coolant Hub coordinates pumps, valves and sensors to allocate cooling according to demand. Its wider thermal system includes a chiller and main and auxiliary radiators.

If the battery is already at the required temperature, the system can direct cooling capacity towards the drive units. When several components are working hard, it must balance their competing needs.

Why the motors are shaped differently

The GT 55 and GT 63 use axial-flux motors developed from technology supplied by Mercedes-owned British specialist YASA.

Their disc-shaped layout places a stator between two magnet-equipped rotors, with magnetic flux running parallel to the shaft. The arrangement offers high torque and power density in a short package.

YASA identifies short copper windings and direct oil cooling as advantages for sustained output, helping remove heat before temperature becomes a constraint.

The rear drive unit combines two motors and their gearboxes, with oil cooling for the motors and gears. Water-cooled silicon-carbide inverters convert the battery’s direct current into the supply the motors require.

Separate rear motors allow driving force to be varied at each rear wheel, changing the turning effect on the vehicle and helping control its path.

Saving capacity for the useful parts of a lap

AMG’s Predictive Performance Manager adjusts power according to the track section, conserving electrical and thermal capacity where extra output offers little lap-time benefit.

A tight downhill sequence, for example, offers less opportunity to exploit full power than an uphill straight. Reducing demand in the former can leave more capacity available for the latter.

Controlling the body without conventional anti-roll bars

The GT 63’s Active Ride Control+ suspension uses a central pump, controlled valves and hydraulically interconnected dampers to generate forces opposing body movement. It replaces conventional anti-roll bars and is optional on the GT 55.

A mechanical anti-roll bar links suspension movement across an axle. It resists roll, but can also transmit a disturbance from one side towards the other. Hydraulic control allows AMG to vary the support according to the driving situation, including pitch under acceleration and braking.

Adjustable air springs control ride characteristics and height. The aim is support during manoeuvres with compliance over uneven roads.

The system still has to manage the SUV’s mass. Its effectiveness requires assessment of grip, ride quality and consistency, alongside how flat the body remains.

There is no confirmed timetable for this combination of motors, battery cooling and active suspension to reach affordable EVs. The demonstrated expansion is within AMG itself, from the electric GT 4-Door Coupe to the GT SUV.

data.title: The best EV sports car yet? Electric Porsche 718 Boxster to debut in early 2027 with sub-three-second sprint
data.description:
Porsche will unveil its first electric 718 Boxster in the first quarter of 2027, with the flagship claimed to reach 100km/h in less than three seconds.

Porsche says the flagship will be the most powerful 718 it has built and will exceed 250km/h on track. All versions of the electric Boxster will be rear-wheel drive.

The iconic sports car maker has yet to confirm power outputs, battery capacity, driving range, pricing or Australian launch timing.

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

READ MORE: Porsche EV plan hits the skids: Petrol replacements for 718 Boxster and Cayman confirmed
READ MORE: No Hyundai-style fake gearboxes for Porsche Cayman or Boxster?
READ MORE: Porsche 718 EV push a precursor to an electrified 911

The appearance of the electrioc Boster is thre latest chapter in something of a saga.

Porsche said in 2022 that the next-generation 718 Boxster and Cayman would be electric-only. In September 2025, as part of a wider pullback from its EV plans, it flagged high-performance petrol variants for the new 718 range. Porsche’s October 2026 strategy listed only electric versions of the two sports cars.

The latest development update focuses entirely on the Boxster and gives no reveal date for the electric Cayman, which Porsche still lists in its product plans.

Porsche has mounted the 800V battery directly behind the seats, where the petrol engine sat in earlier Boxsters. The layout, which Porsche calls E-Core, allows a low seating position and concentrates the battery’s mass near the middle of the car.

“The development of the all-electric 718 Boxster is on the home straight,” said Porsche board member for research and development Michael Steiner.

“In designing this car, we didn’t take the easy route. Instead, we opted for a series of Porsche-typical solutions. A good example of this is the E-Core architecture. It allows for a low seating position and the centre of gravity of a traditional mid-engined car. You can feel that with every metre driven.”

The electric Boxster carries 40 per cent of its weight over the front axle and 60 per cent over the rear. The outgoing petrol Boxster had a roughly 45:55 split.

Porsche says the electric Boxster weighs about the same as its current 911 Cabriolets with the T-Hybrid powertrain. It has yet to publish a kerb weight.

The steering is based on the 911 Carrera GTS set-up. Porsche also drew on the 911 for its wheel, tyre and brake sizing and the electronically controlled PTV+ limited-slip differential. Rear-wheel steering will be available on a Boxster for the first time.

“I would be very satisfied if, when driving the 718 Boxster, our customers can feel how much passion has gone into developing this car and that we have succeeded in transferring the DNA of the combustion-engined 718 into the electric world,” said Frank Moser, who heads Porsche’s 911 and 718 model lines.

Every electric Boxster will come with E-Shift, which simulates a seven-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission. Drivers can switch it on at the touch of a button and choose between automatic changes and manual shifts using the steering-wheel paddles. The shifts vary with the selected drive mode.

Porsche says it briefly increases torque during simulated shifts to deliver the same performance with E-Shift on or off. The mode also recreates the sound of the flat-six from the 981-generation Boxster GTS.

With E-Shift switched off, the paddles select between three levels of regenerative braking.

“It’s really sensational what this car can do,” said two-time world rally champion Walter Röhrl.

“This is where power, braking performance, handling and driving experience all come together perfectly. When you activate the E-Shift function on the steering wheel, the level of driving enjoyment jumps even more. The 718 Boxster gives you more feedback than I’ve ever experienced with any other all-electric car.”

Porsche says the prototypes covered about four million kilometres in more than 20 countries. Temperatures ranged from minus 30 degrees in Sweden to 51 degrees in Death Valley, while test routes ran from 86 metres below sea level to 2750 metres above it.

Engineers evaluated charging performance across five charging standards. They also tested everyday usability and driver assistance systems in city traffic in Las Vegas, Los Angeles and Shanghai.

Porsche will build the electric Boxster at its main plant in Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen. It began releasing a four-part documentary about the car’s development on November 24.

“Starting next year, the all-electric 718 Boxster will offer our customers a compelling entry point into our world of two-door sports cars,” said Porsche chief executive Michael Leiters.

“Our engineers have succeeded in transferring the Boxster’s unique concept to the electric world, further enhancing it in the process. I am thrilled with the level of driving enjoyment the new 718 Boxster offers.”

data.title: Changan Deepal S05 detailed: new entry-level EV and PHEV SUV lays the foundation for Changan’s Australian launch
data.description:
Newly arrived Chinese giant Changan is readying arguably its most important model, the Changan Deepal S05 that will open for orders within weeks.

The S05 will in 2027 form the new entry point to the range, at least until the more affordable Nevo models arrive later in 2027.

The small-to-medium SUV will be offered with battery-electric and plug-in hybrid powertrains across three grades: Pro, Max and AWD Performance.

READ MORE: Changan takes control: Deepal rebranded, nevo confirmed, 5 more models by 2029, Avatr to go it alone
READ MORE: Stop now! Dealers demand new-brand freeze as Chinese EV wave heads for Australia
READ MORE: Best EV and PHEV utes in Australia 2026: The complete guide to electric and plug-in hybrid dual-cabs
READ MORE: Three-pronged Chinese EV assault on Australia! Changan adds Nevo in 2027 as Avatr launches and Deepal switches to factory control

Pre-orders open in December and January, with first customer deliveries due in February.

“This car represents more than just the vehicle,” said Changan Australia head of brand and marketing Andrew Haurissa. “It represents Changan’s ambition on how we are going to market.”

“There are a lot of strong key selling points that are definitely going to shake the market.”

Changan Deepal S05 powertrains

The S05 range includes two electric drivetrains and a plug-in hybrid.

Pro and Max EV: each gets a single-motor RWD setup making 200kW/290Nm. They’re powered by a 68.8kWh LFP battery good for 485km of WLTP range and a claimed 0-100km/h time of 7.5 seconds.

AWD Performance EV: the flagship gets a dual-motor AWD system making a combined 320kW and 502Nm while providing 445km of WLTP range and a 0-100km/h claim of 5.5 seconds.

Max PHEV: uses a 1.5-litre petrol engine driving the front wheels with an electric motor as well. The two produce up to 190kW/300Nm. An 18.4kWh LFP battery delivers 100km of claimed EV-only range and 1060km of combined range. It’s the slowest of the trio, taking 7.9 seconds to hit 100km/h.

Each of the EV variants charges at up to 11kW on AC power and 200kW on DC.

The PHEV takes up to 11kW on AC and 55kW on DC.

Changan claims a 30-80 per cent charge in about 15 minutes for both the EV and the PHEV. Every version also gets 6kW vehicle-to-load capability, allowing household appliances to be powered from a powerpoint.

Changan Deepal S05 equipment

The entry-level S05 Pro comes with:

  • 18-inch alloy wheels and LED headlights
  • frameless doors
  • synthetic leather-accented upholstery
  • power front seats
  • a heat pump
  • automatic climate control
  • a 15.4-inch touchscreen
  • an augmented-reality head-up display
  • wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
  • online sat-nav and DAB radio
  • eight-speaker audio
  • an integrated dashcam and sentry mode

The S05 Max adds:

  • electrically retractable flush door handles
  • roof rails, or an optional panoramic glass roof with power sunshade in their place
  • rear privacy glass
  • heated and ventilated front seats with memory
  • powered driver’s lumbar adjustment
  • a powered front passenger leg rest
  • ambient lighting
  • a power tailgate
  • an auto-dimming rear-view mirror
  • a 50W ventilated wireless phone charger
  • a touchscreen that tilts towards the driver or passenger
  • 14-speaker audio

The S05 AWD Performance builds on the Max with the dual-motor drivetrain and 20-inch alloy wheels.

Safety equipment across all variants includes seven airbags, adaptive cruise control with lane centring, and blind-spot detection. There’s also front and rear cross-traffic alert with braking, a driver fatigue monitor and child presence detection.

A 360-degree camera with a transparent chassis view and front and rear parking sensors are also standard.

The S05 was styled in Changan’s Turin design studio and sits at the smaller end of the medium SUV segment (the S07 is also officially classified as a medium SUV, but it’s bigger).

Its 2880mm wheelbase is designed to maximise rear legroom.

The boot holds 464 litres, and the EVs add a frunk: 159 litres in rear-drive versions and 152 litres in the AWD Performance.

The rear seats split 60:40, and the S05 can tow 1600kg.

Tuned for Australia

Changan says it spent 2000 hours and covered 100,000km testing the S05 on Australian roads from October 2025.

“What we learned helped us tune the car for the conditions that drivers face here every day, and driver assistance was a major focus,” said Changan Australia product manager William Phan.

The S05 carries a five-star Euro NCAP rating, something that should translate to a five-star ANCAP rating (provided there are no structural or equipment changes).

Changan Deepal S05 pricing

Pricing hasn’t been finalised, but Haurissa (somewhat predictably) would only say it would be “competitive”.

If we were guessing, we’d think it’d kick off below $40,000 – but that is purely an educated guess.

Launch offers will be available from day one.

The S05 is the first model under Changan’s new naming, which sees Deepal models rebadged Changan Deepal.

Changan Nevo models and the separate luxury brand Avatr follow in 2027.

data.title: Changan takes control: Deepal rebranded, Nevo confirmed, five more models by 2029 and Avatr to go it alone
data.description:
Chinese car giant Changan has officially launched in Australia as it readies for a big dealer and product expansion.

It is putting its own name on Deepal models – to be branded Changan Deepal – and has confirmed its Nevo sub-brand will arrive as Changan Nevo later in 2027.

The company is also planning three more models in 2028 and two more in 2029. It is tripling its dealer network and has its sights on becoming a top-10 brand.

READ MORE: Stop now! Dealers demand new-brand freeze as Chinese EV wave heads for Australia
READ MORE: Best EV and PHEV utes in Australia 2026: The complete guide to electric and plug-in hybrid dual-cabs
READ MORE: Three-pronged Chinese EV assault on Australia! Changan adds Nevo in 2027 as Avatr launches and Deepal switches to factory control

Its luxury Avatr brand – which has Porsche in its crosshairs – will run separately when it launches in 2027.

“We are building a portfolio, not just launching products,” said Changan Australia head of brand and marketing Andrew Haurissa.

Following the GWM playbook

The strategy to some extent mirrors that of rival GWM.

What started as Haval soon became GWM Haval.

And GWM now sells its Haval, Tank, Ora and Cannon models with the GWM badge front and centre, so the parent brand does the heavy lifting on recognition while each sub-brand keeps its own identity.

Haurissa said the cars would carry “Changan being the brand name and Deepal being the model name”.

Nevo – the company’s youth-focused brand – will follow the same approach.

The current range is now known as the Changan Deepal S07 and Changan Deepal E07, soon to be joined by the new Changan Deepal S05, a car that was supposed to be on sale many months ago.

Once sales start, a Changan badge will go on the left of the tailgate and the model name on the right.

“We want to build recognition over time,” said Haurissa.

“We are not looking to position every product in the same way, and we are not looking to compete on price alone. Each brand must have its own identity, audience, positioning and reasons to exist.”

That’s the opposite of Chery, which runs Chery, Omoda, Jaecoo and Lepas as separate brands with little crossover between them.

Similarly, Geely operates Zeekr, Polestar and Volvo independently of the parent company’s mainstream brand.

Avatr goes it alone

The exception is Avatr.

“The Avatr brand will be the only standalone brand from the Changan Group here in Australia,” said Haurissa.

He described it as “a more premium proposition built around emotive luxury, progressive design and intelligent technology”.

He likened Avatr’s relationship with Changan to Porsche’s place in the Volkswagen family; clearly Porsche is one of the lofty targets the brand hopes to hit.

Avatr will be positioned against the German luxury brands, but with a different focus.

“The Germans focus on the engineering side of things. This focuses on design and performance,” he said.

Avatr is a joint venture involving battery giant CATL, with Huawei as a technology partner overseas.

However, Australian cars won’t run Huawei’s software.

They will instead get a localised operating system called AvatrOS.

Pricing is expected to start north of $60,000, with equipment levels, tech and performance at the heart of the sales pitch.

Avatr’s first model, the 07L large electric SUV, is due in the first half of 2027. The 06T electric wagon follows later in the year.

Nevo next

Haurissa said Deepal would target “intelligent, accessible new energy mobility, with a focus on dynamic performance, for the upper mainstream category”.

Nevo will sit beneath it as “a more youthful, accessible new energy vehicle offering, coming later in 2027”.

That means the new S05 is Changan’s entry point only until Nevo arrives.

The Q05 small SUV is the likely first Nevo.

Australians have already met a Nevo without knowing it: the Deepal E07 sold here is badged as a Nevo in China.

A Changan light commercial vehicle brand is also “under consideration”.

Deepal returns to factory control

Deepal launched in Australia in late 2024 through independent distributor Inchcape, which also looks after Subaru Down Under.

It started with the S07 mid-size electric SUV and later added the unusual E07 SUV-ute mash-up it refers to as the multitruck.

Changan and Inchcape last month agreed to end that arrangement.

The factory-backed operation is taking over in a transition period that runs until 31 March 2027.

“It’s good to acknowledge Inchcape for fostering the Deepal brand over the last 24 months,” Haurissa said. “That has become our building block for today’s progress.”

Deepal sales have been modest so far.

But the plan is for that to change.

Haurissa said being a factory-direct distributor would give Changan “a bit more room to play with”.

Existing models – the S07 and E07 – will get more standard equipment as part of a model update, and pricing is still being reviewed.

There will also be launch offers from day one, all with the aim of arriving with a splash and growing sales.

Changan says it hasn’t set local sales targets yet, but that they’re coming soon.

Updated Changan Deepal S07 on the way

The Deepal S07 – soon to be Changan Deepal S07 – will be updated for 2027, and Changan admits the current car hasn’t always won fans.

“We got some pretty direct feedback: the most annoying car in Australia,” said Changan Australia product manager William Phan, referring to the poorly calibrated advanced driver assistance (ADAS) systems.

“We heard you, and we’ve taken that feedback on.”

As part of the 2027 update the revised S07 gets new two-tone yellow and orange paint options, frequency-selective dampers aimed at improving the ride and a switch to an LFP (lithium iron phosphate) battery in the EV, with up to 500km of WLTP range.

Tripling the dealer network

Changan is aiming to triple its dealer coverage to about 60 by the end of 2027, and every dealership will carry Changan branding as the dominant feature.

“We have already achieved more than halfway of our 2027 goal,” said Haurissa.

It’s not yet clear how many existing Deepal dealers will carry over; the company said negotiations were continuing and the outcome would depend on each market area.

The first appointments are due in December and January. Changan wants 30 dealers in place when deliveries start in February, with a second round of appointments in March.

“Our dealer expansion strategy is ambitious, but deliberately measured,” Haurissa said. “We have the ambition to build something significant here in Australia, but we also have the discipline to build it.”

Top-10 ambitions

Speaking of ambition, Changan is lacking nothing on that front when it comes to sales.

Asked whether Changan could become a top-10 brand in Australia, Haurissa said: “I think there’s an opportunity, yeah.”

He benchmarked Changan’s ambitions against the established Japanese brands rather than value players such as MG. He said Changan wasn’t chasing fast growth.

“We are looking more towards long term, so even if the ascent is not as fast as what other competitors might look like, I think we will definitely be competing in due time.”

Changan Australia managing director Bryan Guan said the company’s product roadmap through to 2029 would bring more choice across different segments and powertrains.

“Looking further ahead, we plan to bring three more models in 2028, followed by a further two models in 2029,” Mr Guan said.

“We know that building a successful brand takes time. This is not just the beginning of a new brand in Australia. It is the beginning of a long-term journey.”

Changan traces its roots to 1862 and has been building vehicles for about 45 years.

It has sold more than 30 million vehicles and has design studios in Italy, Germany and Japan, engineering teams in the UK, and long-running joint ventures with Ford and Mazda.

The first new arrival is the Changan Deepal S05 medium SUV, offered as an EV and a plug-in hybrid.

Pre-orders for the S05 and S07 open in December and January, with first deliveries in February. Changan will then announce new products at the Melbourne Motor Show in April, followed by an end-of-financial-year sales push in May.

data.title: Jetour 10 and Jetour 20 SUVs lead latest Chinese brand launch: Aussie push also includes PHEV 4×4 wagon and luxury ute
data.description:
Adventure-focused Chinese brand Jetour has announced its Australian plans, and the ambitious newcomer says it’s not here to fight on price.

Jetour, the SUV and ute brand owned by Chery, has used its Australian debut in Sydney to lay out an ambitious plan that involves pure ICE vehicles as well as a family of plug-in hybrid SUVs and a luxury and performance-focused ute.

Two plug-in hybrid SUVs arrive in early 2027, a luxury off-roader and a high-powered ute follow later that year, and the brand expects seven models by the end of 2028.

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

READ MORE: Jetour TX electric SUV launches: Chery-owned SUV brand is coming to Australia and this is its first EV
READ MORE: New 575kW Jetour Traveller 7 revealed: Rugged PHEV packs 245km EV range as Chinese brand prepares for Australia

Jetour insists it’s not all about selling in big numbers but says it could sell up to 2000 cars a month from its first two arrivals, the Jetour 10 (badged T1 overseas) and Jetour 20 (known as the T2 overseas).

But on a luxury boat on Sydney Harbour for the media and dealer launch, its executives were just as keen to separate Jetour from the many Chinese brands that have arrived in Australia in recent years.

“If you think Jetour is cheap, I think no need to continue our discussion,” Jetour International executive vice president Yan Jun said.

Jetour 10 and Jetour 20 lead the charge

Jetour’s first two models are known globally as the T1 and T2. In Australia they’ll be called the Jetour 10 and Jetour 20.

Both are boxy, chunky-looking mid-size SUVs on a 2800mm wheelbase. The Jetour 20 is the larger and more rugged of the two, at just over 4.8 metres long and around two metres wide. It also carries a tailgate-mounted spare wheel.

The 10 is more city focused – think Toyota RAV4 and Subaru Forester – but still with an adventurous spirit.

The 20 is more about exploring and adventuring beyond the city limits.

Jetour Motor Australia managing director Johnny Fang said the pair would be the cars “most of our Australian customers first get to know us” by, and the “main volume and profit maker” for dealers.

Certification documents show the line-up will include 1.5-litre turbo-petrol plug-in hybrids, in front-drive and all-wheel-drive forms.

A 2.0-litre turbo-petrol version without the plug-in tech is also listed.

The most potent Jetour 20 PHEV has three electric motors and a combined maximum of 445kW, so it won’t be short of punch.

All-wheel-drive versions use what Jetour calls XWD, an intelligent all-wheel-drive system that adapts to different surfaces without the driver changing settings.

PHEVs are rated to tow up to 1600kg braked, and the petrol-only model 1900kg.

Pre-sales and first deliveries are both due in the first quarter of 2027, with the brand planning for first deliveries in March.

Pricing hasn’t been confirmed. Mr Fang said the full Jetour range would sit between $50,000 and $100,000.

A ute, and a “Lamborghini”

The more interesting Jetour models come later.

In the fourth quarter of 2027 Jetour plans to bring the G700, a large and very powerful plug-in hybrid off-roader, along with a ute version of the same vehicle.

The SUV will be badged simply 700 in Australia while the ute will be the 700P.

“I’m particularly looking forward to bring a Jetour ute to Australia,” Mr Fang said.

Don’t expect a Hilux rival, though.

Mr Yan said the G700 and its pick-up sibling had been benchmarked against the GMC Hummer EV rather than traditional workhorses.

“It’s not a working pickup,” he said. “It has almost 1000 horsepower. All luxury interior … a pickup almost three tonne … PHEV, acceleration 4.6 seconds (to 100km/h).”

He made it clear the 700P was not all about outselling the Toyotas and Fords of the off-road world.

“For me, maybe G700 is a Lamborghini; Lamborghini never push in numbers,” Mr Yan said.

“Maybe we can reach a good volume, but not a big volume … but that definitely helps us to strengthen our premium image.”

One of the big party tricks with the 700 SUV is its ability to float like a boat for 20 minutes.

And whereas the 10 and 20 use a more car-like monocoque construction, the 700 and 700P ride on a ladder-frame chassis.

Battery EVs in the Jetour mix

Jetour has confirmed three more models for 2028, taking the range to seven. One is a small SUV, and the company says it will be fully electric.

The first Jetour EV, the TX SUV, has just launched in China and would be a logical candidate for Australia.

Given rising EV demand in Australia – and tightening CO2 emissions regulations – Mr Yan suggested it could arrive sooner than planned.

“Once we are ready, we for sure will launch as soon as possible the first BEV of Jetour,” Mr Yan said.

He added the brand would not rush it at the expense of quality: “Not push, not fast, and lose the quality, the standard, don’t make mistake.”

Up to 2000 sales a month

Jetour’s executives were reluctant to talk numbers, but they gave some clues as to where the brand could sit in the increasingly competitive – and changing – Australian car market.

“I think our two products here in Australia, if we do a good job, we should make like … 1500 to 2000 units per month,” Mr Fang said.

That’s between 18,000 and 24,000 sales a year from two mid-size SUVs. It’s an ambitious target for a new brand in a market of about 1.2 million sales a year that isn’t growing, even as the number of brands competing keeps rising.

Mr Fang said that figure depended on dealers – Jetour wants to launch with around 60 – after-sales service and availability of parts, something the brand has high on its agenda.

He insisted dealer profitability mattered more than outright volume.

“Dealer profitability is the number one KPI my boss gave to me,” Mr Fang said. He added that each dealer needed to sell 30 to 35 cars a month to break even.

“The last country I worked in, my boss never pushed me for volume. I sell only 30 per cent of the volume compared to other brands. But I’m making money, they are losing money.”

It’s a hot topic right now in Australia.

Some dealers have shut up shop and others are shedding staff as margins get thinner and competition ramps up.

It prompted the Australian Automotive Dealer Association (AADA) this month to call for a pause on any new brands entering the market.

No price wars for Jetour

A theme ran through the night: Jetour does not want to be lumped in with the price-cutting that has characterised many Chinese brands in Australia.

“Everybody says it’s a huge competition here, but we’re not afraid,” Mr Fang said. “And also, we don’t have any plan to [join a] price war here … We want to sell experience.”

Mr Yan was more pointed about some of the brands that have come before Jetour.

“Some brands easily come and easily out … they have no long-term vision,” he said.

“The quality is not good enough. No service, no spare parts. If you want to change some parts, maybe you need to wait two to three months.”

He said Jetour would rather delay its launch than open showrooms without parts in place.

“Once you open the showroom, once you start the sales, once our car is driving on the road, spare parts for customers … it’s the basic.”

Jetour also plans to leave prices out of its advertising, a deliberate move borrowed from premium brands.

Separate from Chery, and not calling itself premium

Jetour is part of the sprawling Chery Group, which in Australia already includes Chery, Omoda, Jaecoo and Lepas, with more brands on the way.

But Mr Yan said Jetour would operate entirely separately, with its own subsidiary, dealers and showrooms.

“Even one dealer group, but showroom must be separated … Cannot mix. Because the image, reputation, everything is totally different,” he said.

He likened Chery to Toyota, as the mainstream “mother brand”, and Jetour to Jeep within the Stellantis group.

Jetour stops short of calling itself a premium brand, though Mr Yan made it clear that’s where it wants to be seen.

“We never say we are premium, because it’s not allowed to say Jetour is a premium brand of Chery,” he said.

“But it’s a matter of the impression of the customer … we don’t have cheap cars, we don’t have sedans, so it’s a special brand.”

Australia a key market for Jetour

Jetour says Australia is its second most important right-hand-drive market after the UK. It also sees an open, competitive market as a good proving ground for a brand that wants to be global.

“Australia has very restricted regulations for any new players to come in, but once you are qualified, we have here 100 per cent free competition,” Mr Fang said.

The brand began studying the Australian market in June 2025. It registered its local subsidiary in March 2026, started testing cars on Australian roads in June and began building its local team in August.

Jetour says it has invested $200 million in development work, covering performance, safety, features and technology.

Its template for Australia is South Africa, another right-hand-drive market, which it entered in 2024. Mr Fang said it took four per cent of the market in its first full year there.

Jetour: A brief history

Jetour is Chery’s adventure-focused brand. Originally developed within the group’s commercial-vehicle arm, it became part of Chery Automobile in 2024. It is a brand focused on travel and adventure, which it markets under the banner of “Travel+”.

Mr Fang said the brand name combines the Chinese “Jie”, meaning speed and success, with “tour”, meaning journey.

Jetour says it has sold more than 2.6 million vehicles since launch.

The brand says it now sells in more than 100 countries through more than 2000 sales and service outlets.

Its design is led by former Ford Australia designer Andrew Collinson, Jetour’s vice president of design.

He says the brand’s look for Australia is built around the idea of being “solid”.

“When Australians give the highest praise, in the most understated way, they call it solid. A solid effort. A solid bloke,” Mr Collinson said.

That extends to colours named after Australian locations, such as the Jetour 20’s hero shade, Sapphire Coast Blue, and a factory matte Snowy Mountain Silver.

data.title: Wings clipped! Next-gen BYD Atto 1 ruled out for Australia in 2027
data.description:
BYD has ruled out bringing its new-generation Atto 1 to Australia in 2027, sticking with the current electric hatchback that has become the country’s cheapest new car at $19,990 drive-away.

The substantially larger second-generation model went on sale in China in October as the Seagull, switching to rear-wheel drive, adding a fifth seat and offering BYD’s Flash Charging technology on higher grades.

But when EV Central asked BYD Australia chief operating officer Stephen Collins whether the new model would come here in 2027, his answer was blunt: “No.”

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

READ MORE: History made! $19,990 BYD Atto 1 becomes Australia’s cheapest new car as EV price war hits new low
READ MORE: BYD Atto 1: Price, range and specifications
READ MORE: 2025 BYD Atto 1 Premium Review: Australia’s cheapest EV is also a decent city car with clever design and real driving character. But will anyone buy it?

“We’re happy with the current one,” Collins said. “We’re selling the current Atto … really strongly, so we’re happy with that.”

The Atto 1 is one example of how quickly BYD is turning over models in China while selling earlier versions overseas. Australia has only recently received the substantially reworked Atto 3 Evo, which brought a bigger battery, more range and faster charging.

BYD had already shown a separate, all-new and considerably larger Atto 3, known as the Yuan Plus in China, at the Beijing motor show in April. Collins indicated there was no immediate plan to replace the Evo here with that model.

Collins also confirmed the Sealion 8 EV and the larger Fang Cheng Bao Ti9 SUV were off the Australian agenda for now, and explained the Brazilian-built Mako compact ute had been ruled ute on business-case grounds.

“We can’t make the Mako work … as a business case,” Collins said. Asked whether that came down to the Brazil sourcing he said: “There’s a whole host of reasons.”

On-sale in Australia only since November 2025, the current BYD sold 4914 examples of the Atto 1 in Australia in the first 10 months of 2026, putting it ahead of the brand’s larger Dolphin hatchback on 3894.

The Atto 1 finished third in the light-car segment in October with 443 deliveries, down from 633 in September. The Geely EX2 electric hatch led the segment in October with 1350, followed by the MG3 on 946.

The $19,990 drive-away deal applies to the entry-level Atto 1 Essential, which undercut the petrol-powered Kia Picanto when BYD introduced the offer in September. Eligible retail orders must be placed by December 15, with delivery generally required by December 31.

The Australian Essential has a 65kW motor driving the front wheels and a 30kWh Blade battery good for a claimed 220km of WLTP range.

The Premium also drives the front wheels, but steps up to 115kW and a 43.2kWh battery for 310km of claimed WLTP range. Both are four-seaters and use torsion-beam rear suspension.

The new Seagull is 425mm longer at 4205mm, with an extra 150mm between the axles. Moving the motor to the rear frees up space for a 94-litre front boot, while the torsion beam gives way to independent multi-link rear suspension.

Its 85kW and 95kW motor options sit between the outputs of the two Australian Atto 1 grades.

BYD claims 320km or 420km of range in China, depending on battery size, under the local CLTC test. It also claims the larger-battery versions can charge from 10 to 70 per cent in five minutes on compatible Flash Charging hardware.

data.title: BMW cranks up the electric speed and luxury as Alpina’s new flagship breaks cover … and 300km/h!
data.description:
BMW’s first electric Alpina is taking shape alongside a V8-powered luxury limousine that has already exceeded 300km/h during testing in Italy.

An i7-based prototype has been spotted testing as BMW prepares to unveil the first production model from its newly acquired Alpina brand in 2027, opening a fresh chapter for a name long associated with rapid, petrol-powered grand tourers.

The electric version has yet to be officially detailed. BMW’s latest release and accompanying video focus on its V8 sibling, giving an insight into the performance and comfort targets likely to shape both versions. Australian availability and pricing remain unannounced.

READ MORE: Best luxury EVs in Australia 2026: Premium electric cars under $100k, $150k, $250k and beyond, priced and compared

READ MORE:450kW BMW iX3 M60 confirmed for Australia: Luxury electric SUV range gains performance flagship
READ MORE: BMW iX4 revealed: Neue Klasse electric coupe SUV confirmed for Australia from $103,900 with up to 828km range
READ MORE: BMW i7 EV flagship overhauled: But has enough been done to keep pace with the new Mercedes-Benz EQS?

The electric prototype looks similar to the camouflaged petrol sedan, but runs without its four oval exhaust outlets or an obvious engine note. A German registration plate ending in ‘E’ provides another clue, although that designation also applies to eligible plug-in hybrids.

BMWBLOG reports the EV is likely to use the updated i7 M70 xDrive as its starting point, bringing Alpina’s traditional emphasis on effortless performance and cabin refinement to an electric drivetrain.

That would give BMW another contender at the upper end of the luxury EV market, above its existing i7 range and below the Rolls-Royce Spectre in the group’s broader portfolio.

BMW has positioned the relaunched Alpina brand between its top-end BMW models and Rolls-Royce, with greater scope for personalisation alongside its performance and comfort upgrades.

For Australian buyers, the updated mainstream i7 60 xDrive has been announced at $306,900 before on-road costs, with a fourth-quarter 2026 launch.

Its dual-motor powertrain produces 400kW and 745Nm, while claimed WLTP range extends to 727km. Any Alpina derivative would be expected to command a substantial premium.

The official Nardò footage suggests Alpina’s engineers are concentrating as much on how the new flagship behaves at speed as how quickly it gets there.

In the film, BMW Alpina boss Oliver Viellechner described the cars internally as “distance-shrinking machines”, explaining that high-speed performance must come with exceptional comfort.

The camouflaged sedan retains Alpina’s familiar 20-spoke wheels, paired with tyres developed specifically for the car. Viellechner says a foam insert helps maintain a smooth ride at high speeds while preserving precision and safety.

BMW says the development program also brings together an aerodynamically optimised body and suspension tuned for both comfort and dynamic capability. The V8 receives specific engine management and accelerator calibration, along with revised transmission tuning.

After the high-speed run, Viellechner praised the steering feedback and the car’s composure.

“Yet everything still feels sublime and incredibly safe. That’s exactly what our customers want,” he said.

BMW took full control of the Alpina brand at the start of 2026. The first new production model is due to be unveiled next year.

data.title: What’s going on down south? Environmental impact ranks last among Victorian motorists’ next-car priorities
data.description:
Environmental impact ranked last among the factors Victorian motorists consider when choosing their next car, with just 27 per cent citing it as a priority in a survey of 800 drivers.

Fuel efficiency was more than twice as commonly cited, at 61 per cent. Price topped the Victorian Automotive Chamber of Commerce (VACC) survey at 68 per cent, followed by reliability at 63 per cent. Safety ranked fourth at 56 per cent.

Price and safety mattered more to older respondents. Among motorists over 55, 83 per cent cited price and 68 per cent prioritised safety.

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

READ MORE: Do you agree? New study says the big thing stopping Australians buying EVs isn’t range or charging
READ MORE: EV sales trends analysed: Cheaper EVs are having an unexpected effect on buying intentions. It’s not necessarily good news…
READ MORE: Tesla and BYD star: EVs and hybrids take more than half of October sales as petrol and diesel slide

The survey found a distinction between caring about price and wanting the cheapest car. In a separate question about which cost factor mattered most, 39 per cent chose long-term value and 26 per cent chose the lowest running costs.

The lowest upfront price was the top consideration for 18 per cent, followed by resale value at 11 per cent and access to finance or payment plans at six per cent.

“Victorians have become sharp, value-driven buyers,” said VACC chief executive Peter Jones. “They’re doing the maths on what a car costs to own and run over years, not months. Reliability and running costs are front of mind because nobody wants a nasty surprise down the track.”

For electric and hybrid cars, that puts the focus on what buyers pay over the time they keep the vehicle. Purchase price and resale value matter alongside fuel or charging costs.

For a battery-electric car, the running-cost calculation also depends on how much charging the owner can do at home and what they pay for electricity.

Petrol and diesel vehicles accounted for 86 per cent of respondents’ main vehicles. Conventional hybrids accounted for eight per cent, battery-electric cars four per cent and plug-in hybrids two per cent.

The published results give no breakdown of which powertrains respondents intend to buy next.

New-vehicle sales capture a different part of the market. VACC reported that battery-electric vehicles accounted for 27.2 per cent of Victorian new light-vehicle sales in August 2026, with 7804 deliveries, up 153.8 per cent on the same month a year earlier.

Nationally, battery-electric cars accounted for 23.1 per cent of new-vehicle deliveries in October 2026, up from 7.3 per cent a year earlier.

Most survey respondents were some way from making their next purchase. Five per cent expected to buy within six months and 13 per cent within six to 12 months. Another 24 per cent expected to buy in one to two years, 29 per cent were looking two years or more ahead and 29 per cent had no plans to buy.

data.title: Off the list: New Nissan NX7 rival for BYD Sealion 6 looks set to miss Australia despite China model push
data.description:
Nissan’s new NX7 plug-in hybrid SUV appears set to bypass Australia, denying the Japanese brand a potential BYD Sealion 6 rival as it turns to China to rebuild its local line-up.

EV Central understands right-hand-drive production may not be planned for the five-seat SUV, leaving it outside Nissan Australia’s current product plans.

Nissan Australia declined to comment on the NX7’s local prospects.

READ MORE: Best EVs to buy in Australia 2026: The ultimate guide to affordable electric cars at every price

READ MORE: Nissan unveils two PHEV concepts in Beijing, including a 4×4 Toyota Prado rival already under study for Australia
READ MORE: Frontier Pro becomes Navara Pro: Nissan confirms China-built PHEV ute for Australia with 300kW and 3.5-tonne towing
READ MORE: Nissan Frontier Pro coming to Australia: Plug-in hybrid ute will fight the BYD Shark 6 and lead a China-sourced electric new model attack

The apparent omission would leave Nissan without a promising new contender in Australia’s hugely competitive medium SUV market, where plug-in hybrids are giving established brands and Chinese newcomers another avenue to attract buyers.

It also highlights the limits of Nissan’s expanding Chinese sourcing strategy: access to a growing range of electrified vehicles does not automatically translate into Australian showroom availability.

In its latest financial results presentation, Nissan confirmed it was exploring plans to export the NX7 plug-in hybrid and the production version of the Terrano Concept, but did not identify their intended export markets.

The NX7 opened for pre-orders at the Nissan Day event in Zhuhai on November 13, ahead of its formal Chinese launch at the Guangzhou motor show on November 27.

Three variants carry Chinese pre-sale prices ranging from 129,900 ($29,400) to 149,900 yuan ($33,900), although those prices do not indicate what an Australian version would cost.

The NX7’s headline attraction is a substantial 40.9kWh CATL lithium iron phosphate battery, fitted across the range, delivering a claimed 320km of electric driving under China’s CLTC testing regime.

Its plug-in hybrid powertrain combines a 73kW 1.5-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine with a 170kW electric motor. Claimed combined range is 1666km, although the Chinese laboratory figures should not be read as Australian real-world expectations.

Measuring 4785mm long, up to 1932mm wide and 1665mm high, with a 2815mm wheelbase, the NX7 offers the size and powertrain configuration to compete with family-focused plug-in SUVs such as the BYD Sealion 6 and Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV.

The production model follows the Urban SUV PHEV Concept shown at April’s Beijing motor show alongside the more rugged Terrano PHEV Concept.

The NX7’s uncertain Australian prospects contrast with Nissan Australia’s confirmed plans for the China-built Navara Pro PHEV ute.

Due locally in 2027, the Navara Pro will become Nissan Australia’s first plug-in hybrid, with Australia and New Zealand its first right-hand-drive markets.

Nissan’s local management has also confirmed more China-sourced vehicles will follow, although the additional models have yet to be named.

The Terrano is among the vehicles being considered for Australia and would provide a different proposition to the road-focused NX7, targeting buyers seeking a more rugged electrified SUV.

However, its Australian introduction remains unconfirmed. Nissan has promised to unveil the production version within a year of the concept’s April 2026 debut.
